metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness TUI explicit /rename writes durable log-only session/title records without opening a model turn; the DSH parser skips those records and maps only the final normal turn to working then ready.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 supports a no-model human command surface, and the installed @tomowang/dsh-tui 0.8.1 profile exposes explicit `/rename <title>`. The TUI parser intercepts `/rename` before ordinary text reaches `actions.send`. With a non-empty explicit title, the handler calls `sessionTitle.rename()` directly. It does not call the model. The mounted @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-title service appends a durable, log-only `session/title` record whose source is `user`. The service documentation states that this record never enters derived model messages, the system prompt, tool schemas, or the request prefix. The recipe uses the explicit-argument form twice. It does not use bare `/rename`, because the TUI documents that the bare form makes an auxiliary model call.

The two exact title records make the negative assertion non-vacuous. If the TUI stopped recognizing `/rename`, either the exact `session/title` records would be absent or the slash text would become real user input and create extra turns. The transcript assertions reject both outcomes. A final exact-word prompt produces the only real `user/message`, `turn/start`, and completed `turn/end`, which proves that the session remains usable after the command window.

The DSH adapter watches the v3 compressed session log under the DSH sessions root. Its parser maps `turn/start` to working, a real `user/message` to working, and a completed `turn/end` to ready. `session/title` is not a state-driving record in `recordHandlers`; the parser skips unknown record types. The two slash commands therefore leave the session ready. The final normal prompt supplies the only ready -> working -> ready arc. The spec also rejects waiting transitions and tool calls. This satisfies every scenario observable.

The driver declares and implements `slash`, `send`, `wait_turn`, and `sleep`. The recipe needs no missing primitive. Its 4-second command intervals match the common sibling slash delays. Its 10-second final settle matches the longest committed sibling delay for this scenario. The 300-second timeout matches the existing local DeepSeek Harness model recipes.

## Vacuous-pass check

This cell could pass from stale data if the driver selected a prior transcript containing the same two title records and one normal turn. The driver's fresh per-run cwd, pre-launch marker, header-cwd match, and session-ID contract are load-bearing preconditions. The exact two title records prevent the more direct vacuous case in which the slash steps do nothing.
caveats: Vacuous-pass condition: a stale transcript with the same two exact user-sourced titles and one completed normal turn could satisfy the cell. The fresh cwd, pre-launch marker, header-cwd match, and session-ID contract are load-bearing recipe preconditions.

Load-bearing environment precondition: the active `tui` profile must contain @tomowang/dsh-tui 0.8.1 or later and mount @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-title. Re-probe the TUI package version and `dsh --profile tui --dump-config` at record time.
Use only explicit `/rename <title>`. Bare `/rename` makes an auxiliary title-generation model call and would invalidate the no-LLM premise.

The daemon verdict is provisional for live compressed-log flush timing. Installed source proves the log-only append and parser behavior, but the recording must confirm both title records reach the harvested transcript before teardown.
This recipe uses a title mutation as the durable proof that each synchronous command executed. The mutation remains outside model history and does not open a turn.

sources.note: Official DeepSeek Harness command documentation: human slash commands run without becoming model messages; direct command output stays outside model history.
Primary TUI documentation lists `/help` and `/rename [title]`, and distinguishes explicit rename from the bare form that generates a title with a model call.
Installed 0.8.1 command parser recognizes `/rename` before ordinary prompt submission.
Installed explicit-title handler calls sessionTitle.rename directly; only the bare form calls generateSessionTitle.
rename() appends `session/title` with the normalized title, empty messageSeqs, and source.kind=user.
Official installed package documentation states that session/title is durable log-only state and never enters model requests or their derived inputs.
Declares the FilesUnderRoot source over compressed DSH transcripts and session.lock-based PID binding.
Maps real turn/start, user/message, assistant usage, and completed turn/end records; skips unrecognized session/title records so they cannot drive state.
Declares and implements slash, send, wait_turn, and sleep; isolates transcript selection by fresh marker and exact cwd.

preconditions: dsh >=0.1.5-rc.2 is installed and on PATH
the active tui profile contains @tomowang/dsh-tui 0.8.1 or later and mounts @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-title; re-probe the package version and `dsh --profile tui --dump-config` at record time
LM Studio is listening at http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 with qwen/qwen3.5-9b loaded
irrlichd is recording the deepseek-harness adapter
setup: The driver creates a fresh per-run cwd and a pre-launch transcript marker, then launches `dsh --profile tui` in tmux.
A temporary patch selects LM Studio and qwen/qwen3.5-9b without modifying the installed profile.
The driver resolves only a readable post-marker transcript whose session header cwd matches the run cwd.

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: the post-marker DSH session is born ready and remains ready during both explicit rename commands
the harvested transcript contains exactly two user-sourced session/title records with the two recipe titles
the transcript contains exactly one real human user/message, one turn/start, and one completed turn/end
the final normal prompt drives the only ready -> working -> ready arc and the session never enters waiting
the transcript and curated event stream contain no tool call
the replay summary reports qwen/qwen3.5-9b and non-zero cumulative tokens
recipe.scope_note: Uses 4-second holds after each synchronous command, matching the common sibling slash delays, and a 10-second final settle, matching the longest committed sibling delay for this scenario.
